## claude.ai Dropbox
# Claude App MCP LLM Boot Instructions

You are the assistant for Dropbox's Claude App MCP server. Your goal is to help users complete Dropbox tasks quickly and correctly while minimizing friction.

## Customer Use Cases

This app is best at helping users do these Dropbox workflows:

- Browse folder contents and paginate through large directories.
- Find files quickly using plain-language search terms and then open files with follow-on tools.
- Inspect file metadata (size, type, timestamps, IDs, sharing context).
- Check signed-in Dropbox identity, team/account context, and namespace-root context.
- Read text content from supported files up to 5 MiB, and provide a usable Dropbox link even when text extraction fails.
- Generate single-use temporary download links when the user explicitly needs direct file download URLs.
- Generate file previews with thumbnail and "open in Dropbox" experiences.
- Create folders in the right destination before saving artifacts.
- Create new text files directly in Dropbox.
- Create share links for files/folders and return the effective sharing settings.
- Inspect and list existing shared links.
- List, inspect, and create Dropbox file requests.
- Move, rename, copy, and delete Dropbox files/folders after explicit confirmation.
- Check the status of long-running move, copy, and delete jobs.

When users ask "what can you do?", summarize these use cases in plain language before taking action.

## Not Supported (Do Not Advertise)

- Editing or overwriting existing file content in place.
- Saving URL-hosted files directly into Dropbox.
- Uploading local/binary artifacts via `upload_file`.
- Permanent file deletion or wipe workflows. `delete` moves items to the user's Dropbox "Deleted files" area only.
- Reliable text extraction for supported files via `fetch`; extraction may still fail for some files, in which case the tool error may include a usable link.
- E-signature initiation or signing workflows.
- Actions outside Dropbox content management and sharing.

## devonthink
CRITICAL — Database package safety: DEVONthink databases are stored as packages (.dtBase2) or sparse images (.dtSparse, .dtArchive). Never modify, rename, move, or delete files inside a database package directly via the filesystem. All record and content operations must go through this MCP server or, as a fallback, via AppleScript. Direct filesystem manipulation will corrupt the database and cause irreversible data loss.

Batch operations: Use the uuids array parameter instead of sequential single-record calls for tag, update, move, trash, duplicate, replicate, and export operations. Batch mode is faster, reduces round trips, and returns a summary with succeeded/failed counts.

Avoiding duplicates: Use lookup_records (by name, URL, path, filename, or comment) before create_record to check whether a record already exists.

Content editing: Prefer update_record_content with mode append or insert over replace for large documents. Replace mode requires sending the entire new content and risks accidental data loss if the content is incomplete.

Group hierarchies: Use create_group_path to create nested group structures in a single call (like mkdir -p) rather than sequential create_record calls.

AI-powered tools: classify_record and find_similar_records use DEVONthink's built-in AI algorithms and proprietary training data — they provide organizational suggestions that complement, not duplicate, your own capabilities.

Record enrichment: resolve_doi_metadata and resolve_book_metadata can enrich existing records with bibliographic metadata by passing the record's uuid — there is no need to create a new record.

AI exclusion: Records marked as excluded from AI access (excludeFromChat) are protected in two ways. (1) Input protection: any tool that receives such a record's UUID as an argument refuses to operate on it and returns an error. Use when users mention "systems thinking," "systemic," "feedback loops," "unintended consequences," "root cause," "interconnected," or request analysis of complex, multi-factor problems. Scans for all CLAUDE.md files, evaluates quality against templates, outputs quality report, then makes targeted updates. Also use when the user mentions "CLAUDE.md maintenance" or "project memory optimization".
- dataviz: Use this skill whenever you are about to create ANY chart, graph, plot, dashboard, or data visualization, in ANY output medium — an HTML or React artifact, inline SVG, plotting code in any library (matplotlib, plotly, d3, Recharts, …), an image/PNG you will render and upload, or a chart shared into Slack. Read it BEFORE writing the first line of chart code, choosing chart colors, building a stat tile / meter / KPI row, or laying out a dashboard. Produces visualizations that read as one system — elegant, accessible, consistent in light and dark — using a brand-neutral placeholder palette you swap for your own. Teaches a design-system-agnostic method: a form heuristic, a color formula with a runnable validator, mark specs, and interaction rules. Also use for: permissions ("allow X", "add permission", "move permission to"), env vars ("set X=Y"), hook troubleshooting, or any changes to settings.json/settings.local.json files. Do NOT invoke for one-off tasks.
- claude-api: Reference for the Claude API / Anthropic SDK — model ids, pricing, params, streaming, tool use, MCP, agents, caching, token counting, model migration.
TRIGGER — read BEFORE opening the target file; don't skip because it "looks like a one-liner" — whenever: the prompt names Claude/Anthropic in any form (Claude, Anthropic, Fable, Opus, Sonnet, Haiku, `anthropic`, `@anthropic-ai`, `claude-*`, `us.anthropic.*`, `[1m]`); the user asks about an LLM (pricing/model choice/limits/caching) — never answer from memory; OR the task is LLM-shaped with provider unstated (agent/MCP/tool-definition/multi-agent/RAG/LLM-judge/computer-use; generate/summarize/extract/classify/rewrite/converse over NL; debugging refusals/cutoffs/streaming/tool-calls/tokens).
SKIP only when another provider is being worked on (overrides all triggers): OpenAI/GPT/Gemini/Llama/Mistral/Cohere/Ollama named in the query; OR `grep -rE 'openai|langchain_openai|google.generativeai|genai|mistralai|cohere|ollama'` over the project hits (run this grep FIRST if no provider named — don't Read the file).

First looks for a project skill that already covers launching the app; otherwise falls back to built-in patterns per project type (CLI, server, TUI, Electron, browser-driven, library).

## Bugs / UX issues

- **Receipt with No Date** - if a receipt has no date it is hard to find in the receipts view.
- **Category edit scrolls to top.** When a category is edited we always scroll back up to the top of the window.
- **Category dropdown clipped.** The category dropdown in the editor window is out of view when clicked.
- **Refunds counted as spending in PDF/CSV exports.** The PDF and CSV exporters `Math.abs()` amounts, so refunds (negative `total_amount`) are treated as spend instead of netting out. Worst case is `PDFExportService.calculateSubtotal` (`src/lib/services/PDFExportService.ts:176`), which _adds_ `abs(amount)` — a −$25.50 refund + $100 purchase totals **$125.50** instead of $74.50. The display formatters also strip the sign (`PDFExportService.ts:126`, `CSVExportService.ts:134`), so an exported refund prints as a positive purchase. The on-screen Spending report is correct (`spendingReport.ts:135` keeps refunds negative) — only the exports diverge. Note: current behaviour is deliberate and locked in by tests (`PDFExportService.spec.ts:199`, `CSVExportService.spec.ts:106`), so a fix must update those too. Low priority.
- **Blank transaction date hint.** When the transaction date is blank, show the expected date format for someone who is typing.
- **Unknown-sender email is silently dropped.** When a receipt is forwarded from an address not linked to any account, the webhook returns `404` and sends **no** notification — the sender gets no acknowledgement or error and the receipt never appears (`resend/index.ts:378-381`). Resend does not bounce/reply on a webhook error, so any feedback must be an email we send ourselves; deferred because auto-replying to unverified `From:` addresses is a backscatter/spoofing risk (would need SPF/DKIM gating + rate limiting). **End-user docs must flag this:** forward only from a registered email (primary or an additional email in your profile). - **✅ DONE — unauthenticated data-forgery chain closed.** The [Security Remediation PRD](prd-done/prd-security-remediation.md) shipped R2–R5 in `20260717_security_remediation_chain.sql` (+ follow-up `20260718_fix_f3_revoke_anon.sql`) and **verified all five §Verification checks against the live deployment on 2026-07-17**: anon `find_user_by_email` (R4/H1) and `insert_receipt_with_context` (R2/C2) denied, `family_members` reads scoped via an `is_member_of()` SECURITY DEFINER helper (R5/H2), tautological receipts INSERT/UPDATE `WITH CHECK` fixed to `fm.family_id = receipts.family_id` (R3/C3), and webhook signature enforced (R1/C1). Verified with the throwaway `.scratch/verify-security.sh` (uncommitted). PRD moved to `docs/prd-done/`.
- **✅ DONE — family_members self-join closed.** The open `"Users can insert their own membership"` INSERT policy (which, with the `USING(true)` SELECT, let any authed user self-join any family for a whole-tenant breach) was **dropped** in `20260717_security_remediation_chain.sql`. There is now no client membership-write path — legitimate membership goes through the `SECURITY DEFINER` `ensure_default_family()` (bypasses RLS). Verified live 2026-07-17 (self-insert into an arbitrary family rejected). The sanctioned invite-based replacement is designed in [PRD — Family Invitations](prd-family-invitations.md).

The Resend webhook attributes inbound receipts via `find_user_by_email(sender)`, which falls through to those profile columns (`resend/handler.ts`). So an attacker can claim a victim's forwarding/secondary address and have the victim's forwarded receipts ingested into the attacker's account (data leak), or make attribution nondeterministic (`limit 1`) when two profiles claim the same address, or pre-claim an address to poison a future user. Not closed by the webhook-signature fix (abuse is by a legit authed user). Fix: confirm ownership via emailed token before an alias participates in lookup; add a global `UNIQUE(lower(email))` (ideally a normalized `profile_emails` table); prefer exact `auth.users` identity over unverified aliases.
- **✅ DONE — anon-executable seed functions locked down.** `create_default_hierarchy` / `create_default_categories` carried a **direct** `anon` EXECUTE grant (Supabase default privileges), so `anon` could seed rows into empty tenants. `20260717_security_remediation_chain.sql` revoked `FROM PUBLIC`, but live testing showed that missed the direct anon grant (the call still executed, blocked only by a FK) — so `20260718_fix_f3_revoke_anon.sql` added explicit `REVOKE … FROM anon`; `authenticated` keeps its grant (the `CategoryService` caller). Verified live 2026-07-17. **Lesson learned:** on Supabase, `REVOKE … FROM PUBLIC` alone does NOT remove `anon`/`authenticated` — they hold _direct_ grants via default privileges, so revoke those roles explicitly. (Still open: a sweep of any _other_ `SECURITY DEFINER` functions for the same missing REVOKE.)

The union-of-both-years approach (the code is gone — it was never committed, so not in git history; the idea is described in the ADR) is the one salvageable piece if **diverging change bars** are ever built to surface disappeared spend.

Options: (a) pin the CDN tarball (`xlsx@https://cdn.sheetjs.com/xlsx-0.20.3/...` via `overrides`) — clears the CVEs, keeps `.xls` support, but adds a non-npm-registry dep that our `min-release-age` hardening can't gate; (b) migrate to `exceljs` — actively maintained, but **cannot read legacy `.xls`** (xlsx/csv only), so it would drop `.xls` support unless paired with a dedicated BIFF parser (`js-xls`). Decision needed on whether legacy `.xls` is still required. Deferred — the importer is not internet-exposed (users upload their own bank exports), which lowers the practical risk.

Low priority; both are dev/transitive, not shipped to users.

Here's what I found and what I'd recommend.

## First: the web app already does most of this on an iPhone

`src/routes/receipts/+page.svelte:489` is a plain `<input type="file" accept="image/jpeg,image/png,image/heic,application/pdf" multiple>`. On iOS Safari that already opens the native sheet with **Take Photo**, **Photo Library**, and **Choose File** — and HEIC is accepted. So the stated MVP scope (capture or pick a photo → upload to the DB) is *already shipped*, minus polish.

That reframes the question. A native app isn't justified by "take a photo and upload" — it's justified by the things the browser genuinely cannot do on iOS:

| Capability | Mobile web | Native iOS |
|---|---|---|
| Camera + photo library pick | ✅ today | ✅ |
| Home-screen icon | ✅ (needs a manifest — `static/` has only `robots.txt`) | ✅ |
| **Share Extension** ("Share → YFL" from Photos/Mail) | ❌ | ✅ |
| **Background upload** (survives app backgrounding / poor signal) | ❌ | ✅ |
| **Offline queue** (snap now, upload later) | ~ (fragile; iOS evicts storage) | ✅ |
| Multi-shot batch scanning with edge detection (`VNDocumentCameraViewController`) | ❌ | ✅ |
| Face ID lock | ❌ | ✅ |

If none of those matter to you, the honest answer is: **add a web manifest and a "Scan receipt" button, don't build an iOS app.** That's a day of work versus a multi-week project plus a $99/yr Apple Developer account. If the share-sheet + background-upload + document-scanner story is what you actually want (and for receipt capture, the VisionKit document scanner is a real quality jump — auto-crop, deskew, glare handling), native is worth it.

## Your actual question: same repo or new?

**Same repo, as a top-level `ios/` directory.** Reasons specific to this codebase:

1. **The schema is the contract, and it lives here.** `supabase/migrations/` holds the RLS policies the iOS app is entirely dependent on — `20260225_secure_receipts_storage.sql` encodes the `user_id/uuid.ext` storage-path convention, and `20260717_security_remediation_chain.sql` encodes the receipts INSERT `WITH CHECK`. A separate repo means a migration can land here and silently break the iOS client with nothing in either repo's history connecting the two.
2. **Coordinated changes are one PR.** Adding a column, loosening a policy, or changing the ingest contract touches both clients.
3. **The toolchains don't collide.** Xcode/SwiftPM and npm/Vite share nothing. `.gitignore` additions and path-filtered CI are the whole integration cost.
4. **Docs are already centralized here** — `docs/adr/`, `docs/prd-*.md`, `docs/domain-model.md`. The iOS PRD and its ADRs belong in the same place as the ubiquitous-language glossary they consume.

The one thing that would flip this: if you ever want to open-source or hand off one half independently, or if App Store release cadence starts fighting web deploys badly enough that you want separate tags. Neither applies to a family app.

## The decision that matters more than the repo

`ReceiptService.uploadAndCreate()` is a six-step pipeline running **in the browser**: validate → resize → upload to storage → OCR via `/api/ocr/extract` → date correction (`resolveOcrReceiptDate`) → insert → auto-categorize by vendor rule. If the Swift app reimplements that, you have two copies of receipt business logic to keep in lock-step — the exact failure mode your CLAUDE.md already warns about for the Deno `supabase/functions/_shared/` copy. That'd be a third copy.

**Recommendation: extract the post-upload pipeline into a Supabase Edge Function** (say `ingest-receipt`) that takes `{ storagePath, mimeType }` and does OCR → date correction → insert → auto-categorize server-side. Then:

- iOS is genuinely thin: sign in, capture, resize, upload to storage, call one function. Maybe 400 lines of Swift.
- The web app migrates to the same function and *loses* logic rather than gaining a twin.
- It closes backlog item **H3** for free — `/api/ocr/extract` (`src/routes/api/ocr/extract/+server.ts`) currently has **no authentication and no host allow-list on the caller-supplied `fileUrl`** (SSRF + unmetered Mistral spend). An iOS client would have to call it, so you'd be putting a second consumer on a known-open endpoint. Fix it before, or fold it into the Edge Function.

The alternative — MVP where iOS uploads the image and inserts a bare `receipts` row with no OCR, and you edit it on the web later — is a legitimate way to ship in a week and defer this. But it means the iOS app produces second-class receipts, and you'll build the Edge Function eventually anyway.

## Suggested shape, if you go native

**Stack:** Swift + SwiftUI, `supabase-swift` (the official first-party SDK — Auth, Storage, PostgREST, Functions all in one package). iOS 17+ target. VisionKit's `VNDocumentCameraViewController` for capture, `PhotosPicker` for the library. No cross-platform framework — you have one platform and a tiny surface; React Native/Flutter would buy nothing and cost a toolchain.

**Phases:**
- **P0 — decision + prerequisites.** Confirm native vs PWA. Apple Developer Program enrollment ($99/yr, can take days). Decide the auth method (see below). Fix or replace the OCR endpoint.
- **P1 — walking skeleton.** Sign in, pick one photo, upload to `receipts/{user_id}/{uuid}.jpg`, confirm the row appears in the web app. Proves auth + RLS + storage path convention end to end.
- **P2 — capture quality.** VisionKit scanner, HEIC→JPEG, the 2000px/85% resize to match `imageResize.ts`, multi-page batch.
- **P3 — reliability.** Upload queue with retry, background `URLSession`, offline capture.
- **P4 — Share Extension.** "Share → YFL" from Photos and Mail. This is the highest-value native-only feature and worth its own phase.

**Auth is the sharp edge.** Two things to settle up front:
- Your web app has multi-email support and family-scoped RLS. The iOS session must resolve to the same `auth.users` identity, or storage RLS silently hides the family's receipts.
- **App Store Guideline 4.8:** if you offer *any* third-party/social login, you must also offer Sign in with Apple. Email+password only avoids the requirement entirely. Given a family app, magic-link or email/password is simplest — but magic links round-trip through Mail, which is friction on a phone.

**Distribution:** for a family-only app, TestFlight is probably the endpoint — no App Store review for internal testers (up to 100). Caveat: **TestFlight builds expire after 90 days**, so you're re-uploading quarterly forever. Full App Store release avoids that but means review, a privacy nutrition label, and a support URL for an app only your family uses.

---

I'd suggest settling two things before anything else: **(a) is the share-sheet / background-upload / document-scanner set actually what you want, or is a PWA manifest enough?** and **(b) does the ingest pipeline move to an Edge Function first, or does the iOS MVP create OCR-less receipts?**

Say the word and I'll write this up as `docs/prd-ios-receipt-capture.md` with the phases, open questions, and the Edge Function contract spelled out.

That reframing is right, and it points at a specific design rather than a platform choice. Two concrete findings first, because they change the plan.

**HEIC currently defeats the resizer.** `resizeImage()` returns the file untouched for anything that isn't JPEG/PNG (`imageResize.ts:71`), and the receipts input opts *into* HEIC via `accept="…,image/heic,…"` (`receipts/+page.svelte:492`). iOS Safari transcodes a picked photo to JPEG when the `accept` list excludes HEIC, and hands over the raw HEIC when it's included — so today's config takes the one path where a full-size iPhone photo goes to storage and to Mistral unresized. On cellular that's the difference between a ~400KB upload and a ~3MB one. Worth verifying on a real device, but if it holds, dropping `image/heic` from the accept list on the capture screen is a one-line win. (It also interacts with the 5MB image cap in `validateFile` — a 12MP HEIC can brush against it.)

**The root layout owns the nav.** `src/routes/+layout.svelte` is 143 lines of nav chrome + auth gate + `preserveFilters`. Every route inherits it. A chrome-free capture screen needs either a route-group split or a conditional.

## The approach I'd recommend

**One purpose-built route in this app — `/capture` — installed to the home screen as a PWA with `start_url: /capture`.**

The insight is that the PWA manifest lets you ship *two products from one codebase*. Tapping the home-screen icon opens standalone, chrome-free, directly on the capture screen — it looks and behaves like a single-purpose camera app, and never shows the expenses table, the spending report, or the date filters. The full app stays at the normal URL for desktop. Same repo, same auth, same `ReceiptService`, same deploy. No second codebase, no App Store, no $99/yr.

Two alternatives I'd reject:

- **Make the whole app responsive.** Big job, and it doesn't solve your actual complaint. A responsive `/expenses` table is still a dense multi-column grid you don't want on a phone while standing at a till. The problem isn't layout width, it's that a phone session has exactly one job.
- **Separate deployment (`m.yfl…`).** Doubles infra and splits the session cookie/origin, which breaks the shared Supabase auth for no benefit. The manifest gets you the same result for free.

## What's actually on the screen

The design constraint is one-handed, standing up, possibly outdoors, in under five seconds:

- **A single large shutter button** — `capture="environment"` opens the camera directly with no intermediate sheet. A smaller secondary "From library" control (same input, no `capture` attribute) for photos already taken.
- **Immediate return to the shutter.** After a shot, the upload starts in the background and the button is instantly ready again. Capturing five receipts should be five taps, not five upload-wait cycles.
- **A queue strip** below: local thumbnail (from `URL.createObjectURL`, no signed-URL round trip), per-item state — uploading → reading → done/failed — and tap-to-retry on failure.
- **Nothing else.** No nav, no filters, no table.

The pipeline already supports this: `uploadAndCreate()` is fail-soft on OCR, cleans up orphaned blobs on insert failure, and wraps in `withRetry`. What's missing is that it's currently awaited serially per file — the mobile screen needs it fired into a queue with observable per-item state.

## Decisions I need from you

**1. Does the capture screen show OCR results, or is it fire-and-forget?** This is the biggest fork. OCR takes several seconds via Mistral, so "snap → confirm merchant/amount/date → save" turns a 5-second task into a 20-second one. Fire-and-forget ("4 receipts uploaded, review on desktop") is faster and much simpler to build, but means the `suspicious_date` flag and any OCR miss surface later, in a different place, possibly never. My lean is **fire-and-forget for v1** with a passive count of items needing review — but if receipts routinely go unreviewed today, that's the wrong call and inline confirmation earns its cost.

**2. Route-group refactor, or conditional nav?** Clean: move the current layout into `src/routes/(app)/+layout.svelte` and give `(capture)` its own — mechanical but touches every route's path. Cheap: keep one layout and hide the nav when the path starts with `/capture`. I'd do the route group; the conditional accumulates special cases.

**3. Are you willing to install it to the home screen?** The whole design depends on it. Opening `/capture` in a Safari tab still works, but you get browser chrome and lose the standalone feel.

## The one honest limitation

**iOS Safari does not support the Background Sync API.** So "snap five receipts in a parking garage with no signal, pocket the phone, and have them upload later" does not work on web. The best available is holding files in IndexedDB and retrying when the page is next opened — which requires you to actually reopen it. If that scenario is common for you, it's the single strongest argument for native, and worth deciding now rather than discovering in v2.

Everything else on the native-vs-web list — camera, library, home-screen icon, HEIC — the web handles.

## Rough phasing

- **P1 — the screen.** `/capture` route, chrome-free layout, shutter + library buttons, sequential upload with visible per-item state. Fix the HEIC/`accept` issue. Usable end to end.
- **P2 — installable.** `manifest.webmanifest` with `start_url: /capture`, `display: standalone`, icons; apple-touch-icon. **Spike first:** confirm the Supabase session survives in standalone mode across days — an iOS home-screen web app has its own storage container separate from Safari, so you'll log in again on first launch, and I want to see how long the session actually lives before committing to the design.
- **P3 — queue polish.** Parallel uploads with a concurrency cap, retry-on-failure, IndexedDB persistence so a mid-upload app switch doesn't lose the shot.
- **P4 — review loop.** Whatever decision 1 lands on: either an inline confirm sheet, or a "needs review" count that deep-links into the desktop app.

Answer those three and I'll write it up as `docs/prd-mobile-capture.md`.

## Terminology

See [domain-model.md](domain-model.md). A **Family** is the data-scoping unit; a
**Family Member** is a row in `family_members(family_id, user_id, role, status,
is_default)` with `role ∈ {owner, member}` and `status ∈ {active, invited,
removed}`. An **Invitation** (new concept) is a pending, email-addressed offer to
join a family; it is **not** a membership and grants no access until accepted. UI
copy uses "invite" / "family member".

# PRD — Mobile Capture (single-purpose receipt capture on a phone)

- **Status:** Draft
- **Created:** 2026-07-26
- **Surface:** a new chrome-free `/capture` route; a route-group split of
  `src/routes/+layout.svelte`; a web app manifest + icons in `static/`; a queued
  wrapper around the existing `ReceiptService.uploadAndCreate()`.
- **Related:**
  - Backlog **"iPhone camera"** feature — this PRD is its concrete design, and
    deliberately answers it with a web app rather than a native iOS app.
  - [Refactoring backlog](refactoring-backlog.md) — the layout split (D2) is a
    prerequisite, not a nice-to-have.
  - Security **H3** (`/api/ocr/extract` unauthenticated + SSRF) — not caused by
    this work, but this feature adds a second high-traffic consumer of that
    endpoint. See [Security Remediation PRD](prd-done/prd-security-remediation.md).
  - [domain-model.md](domain-model.md) — Receipt, Expense terminology.

## Terminology

See [domain-model.md](domain-model.md). A **Receipt** is a row in `receipts` plus
its stored image; an **Expense** is the computed join of a receipt with its
category. This PRD introduces no new domain concepts — only a second **client
surface** onto the existing receipt-creation pipeline.

Two new UI terms, both presentational:

- **Capture screen** — the `/capture` route: one job, no navigation.
- **Upload queue** — the client-side, in-memory (later persisted) list of files
  in flight, each with its own state. Not a database concept; nothing is queued
  server-side.

## Problem

The app is usable on a phone but was not designed for one. Every route inherits
the full navigation chrome, date filters, and desktop-density tables from
`src/routes/+layout.svelte` (143 lines). The receipts page is a management
console — list, sort, edit, split, reconcile — with upload as one control among
many.

That mismatch matters because the phone use case is not "manage receipts." It is
a single five-second task, performed standing up, one-handed, often on cellular,
immediately after a purchase: **photograph this receipt and make it go away.**
Anything that asks the user to navigate, scroll past a table, or wait for an
upload before taking the next shot is friction at exactly the wrong moment — and
the observable consequence is receipts that never get captured at all.

The naive fix is "make the app responsive." That is a large job and it does not
solve this problem: a responsive `/expenses` table is still a dense multi-column
grid, and the user standing at a till does not want it at any width.

The second naive fix is a native iOS app. Assessed and rejected for v1 — see
**D1**.

## Goals

- Capturing a receipt on a phone is: open icon → tap shutter → done. Five
  seconds, one hand, no navigation.
- Capturing **n** receipts in a row is **n** taps, not **n** upload-wait cycles.
- The capture surface shares one codebase, one deployment, one auth session, and
  one ingestion pipeline with the desktop app.
- The image that reaches storage is resized, regardless of what format the phone
  hands us.
- A failed upload is visible and retryable, never silent.

## Non-goals

- **A native iOS app.** Rejected for v1 (**D1**), with the one scenario that
  would justify it named explicitly under **Risks**.
- **Making the rest of the app responsive.** `/expenses`, `/spending`,
  `/transactions`, `/reconciliation` are unchanged and remain desktop surfaces.
  This PRD adds a route; it does not restyle existing ones.
- **Editing receipts on the phone.** No category assignment, no split, no
  reconciliation, no merchant correction beyond what **R6** decides. Review
  happens on the desktop app.
- **Offline capture.** Explicitly deferred to a later phase and constrained by a
  platform limit (**Risks**). v1 requires a live connection.
- **Changing the ingestion pipeline.** `uploadAndCreate()` keeps its current
  semantics — OCR fail-soft, orphan-blob cleanup, `withRetry`. This PRD wraps it,
  it does not rewrite it. (Moving the pipeline server-side into an Edge Function
  remains a good idea and a separate decision; it is **not** a prerequisite.)
- **Android.** The design is standards-based and should work, but iOS Safari is
  the only target verified.

## Design

### D1 — A PWA route, not a native app (the platform decision)

The existing receipts input (`src/routes/receipts/+page.svelte:489`) is already a
`<input type="file" accept="image/jpeg,image/png,image/heic,application/pdf"
multiple>`. On iOS Safari that already offers **Take Photo**, **Photo Library**,
and **Choose File**. The camera is not the missing capability — the
single-purpose surface is.

A web app manifest lets one codebase ship two products. With `start_url:
/capture` and `display: standalone`, the home-screen icon opens chrome-free,
directly on the capture screen, and never reveals the expenses table or the date
filters. The desktop app stays at the normal URL.

What a native app would add, and why each is insufficient here:

| Capability                          | Web        | Native | Verdict for v1 |
| ----------------------------------- | ---------- | ------ | -------------- |
| Camera capture / photo library      | ✅         | ✅     | No gain        |
| Home-screen icon, standalone chrome | ✅         | ✅     | No gain        |
| HEIC handling                       | ✅ (**D5**) | ✅     | No gain        |
| Share Extension (Photos → app)      | ❌         | ✅     | Real, deferred |
| Background upload                   | ❌         | ✅     | Real, deferred |
| Offline queue                       | ❌ (**Risks**) | ✅ | Real, deferred |
| Document scanner (auto-crop/deskew) | ❌         | ✅     | Real, deferred |

Against that: a native app costs an Apple Developer Program membership
($99/yr), a second toolchain, a second copy of the upload pipeline in Swift — a
third copy of logic that must stay in lock-step, which is the failure mode
`CLAUDE.md` already warns about for the Deno `supabase/functions/_shared/`
duplication — and TestFlight builds that expire every 90 days. The web route
costs one route and a manifest.

**Decision: build the web route.** Revisit natively only if the offline scenario
under **Risks** proves to be a real, recurring need.

### D2 — Route-group split so the capture screen has no chrome

`src/routes/+layout.svelte` currently owns three things at once: the auth gate
(`publicRoutes`, `authChecked`), the nav chrome, and `preserveFilters`. The
capture screen needs the first and none of the rest.

Two options:

- **(a) Route groups.** Move today's layout to `src/routes/(app)/+layout.svelte`
  and give the capture screen `src/routes/(capture)/+layout.svelte`. Auth
  handling is lifted into a shared root layout so it is not duplicated. Route
  groups do not affect URLs, so every existing path is unchanged.
- **(b) Conditional.** Keep one layout and hide the nav when the path starts with
  `/capture`.

**Recommend (a).** Option (b) is one line today and accretes a special case per
divergence — and this PRD is the first of what will be several: the capture
screen also wants a different viewport meta, different safe-area padding, and no
`preserveFilters` subscription. The auth-gate extraction is the only real work;
it is mechanical and independently testable.

### D3 — The screen: one shutter, immediate re-arm

The layout is deliberately impoverished:

- **A single large shutter control**, thumb-reachable in the lower third, using
  `capture="environment"` so it opens the camera **directly** — no intermediate
  sheet.
- **A smaller secondary control** for the photo library — the same input without
  the `capture` attribute, so iOS offers the picker.
- **Immediate re-arm.** Upload starts in the background and the shutter is ready
  again at once. This is the core interaction: capturing five receipts is five
  taps.
- **An upload-queue strip** below the shutter: a local thumbnail per item (from
  `URL.createObjectURL` — no signed-URL round trip), a state label, and
  tap-to-retry on failure.
- **Nothing else.** No nav, no filters, no table, no totals.

### D4 — The upload queue

`uploadAndCreate()` today is awaited per file, serially, with the page's
`uploading` boolean as the only feedback. The capture screen needs per-item state
and concurrency.

Each queue item carries: a client-generated id, the local object URL, and one of
`queued → uploading → extracting → done | failed` (plus the error message for
`failed`). The mapping onto the existing pipeline is direct — `uploading` covers
`prepareFileForUpload` + `uploadToStorage`, `extracting` covers
`extractReceiptDataFailSoft`, `done` is set after
`insertReceiptOrCleanupUpload` returns.

Two properties the existing pipeline already gives us and the queue must not
break: OCR failure still produces a receipt (fail-soft), and a failed insert
removes the uploaded blob (no orphans). A queue item that reaches `failed`
therefore has left nothing behind, and retry is safe.

Concurrency is capped (start at 2) so a burst of captures on cellular does not
saturate the connection and starve the shot in progress.

**The queue is presentation state, not business logic.** The state machine and
the concurrency policy are pure and unit-testable; the Svelte component renders
them. Do not put upload orchestration inside the component.

### D5 — HEIC must not bypass the resizer

`resizeImage()` returns the file untouched for anything that is not JPEG or PNG
(`src/lib/utils/imageResize.ts:71`), and `prepareFileForUpload()` skips the
resize call for the same set (`ReceiptService.ts:203`). Meanwhile the receipts
input opts **into** HEIC via its `accept` list.

The suspected consequence: iOS Safari transcodes a picked photo to JPEG when the
`accept` list excludes HEIC, and hands over the original HEIC when it is
included. If so, today's configuration selects the one path where a full-size
iPhone photo goes to storage and to Mistral **unresized** — roughly a 3MB upload
where a 400KB one would do, on the connection least able to afford it. It also
sits near the 5MB image ceiling in `validateFile()`
(`ReceiptService.ts:170`), so a large capture can be rejected outright.

**This is a hypothesis and must be verified on a real device before it is acted
on** (see **R1**). If confirmed, the capture screen omits `image/heic` from its
`accept` list so iOS converts to JPEG and the file flows through the existing
resizer. The desktop receipts page keeps HEIC in its list — a Mac user may
legitimately upload a `.heic` file, and there the size and bandwidth cost is not
a concern.

Note the asymmetry this creates: two `accept` lists for two surfaces, for a
stated reason. Comment it at both sites.

### D6 — Installability

A manifest (`static/manifest.webmanifest`) with `name`, `short_name`,
`start_url: /capture`, `display: standalone`, theme/background colours, and the
icon set; plus `apple-touch-icon` and viewport/safe-area meta in `app.html`.

**No service worker is required for v1.** iOS supports Add to Home Screen and
honours `display: standalone` from the manifest without one. A service worker is
introduced only if and when offline persistence (P4) is built — adding one
earlier buys nothing and brings a cache-invalidation problem the app does not
currently have.

## Requirements

### R1 — Verify the HEIC hypothesis (do this first)

On a real iPhone, capture through the current receipts input and record: the
`File.type` and `File.size` the browser hands over, whether `prepareFileForUpload`
resizes, and the bytes that land in storage. Repeat with `image/heic` removed
from `accept`. **D5** is contingent on this result; if the behaviour differs from
the hypothesis, revise D5 rather than implementing it as written.

### R2 — Layout split

Per **D2(a)**. Auth gate extracted to a shared root layout; existing nav chrome
and `preserveFilters` move to `(app)`; a minimal `(capture)` layout. No URL
changes, no behaviour change to any existing route.

### R3 — `/capture` route

Per **D3**. Shutter (`capture="environment"`), library control, queue strip,
no chrome. Must render correctly with the on-screen keyboard absent and respect
iOS safe-area insets.

### R4 — Upload queue

Per **D4**. Pure state machine + concurrency policy; component renders it.
Reuses `ReceiptService.uploadAndCreate()` unchanged.

### R5 — Manifest and icons

Per **D6**. Installs to the home screen, opens standalone on `/capture`.

### R6 — Post-capture feedback

**Open — see Open Questions 1.** The default assumed by this PRD is
fire-and-forget: the queue strip is the only feedback, plus a passive count of
receipts awaiting review that deep-links into the desktop app. If inline OCR
confirmation is chosen instead, R6 grows substantially and P3 should be
re-estimated.

## Acceptance criteria

- Tapping the home-screen icon opens the capture screen full-bleed, with no
  browser or app navigation chrome visible.
- Tapping the shutter opens the camera directly — no intermediate action sheet.
- After taking a photo, the shutter is usable again before the upload completes.
  Five receipts can be captured in five taps without waiting.
- Each queued item shows a thumbnail and its current state; a failed item shows
  an error and can be retried, and retrying succeeds once connectivity returns.
- A receipt captured on the phone appears in the desktop `/expenses` list with
  the same family scoping, auto-categorisation, and `suspicious_date` behaviour
  as one uploaded from the desktop. **No divergence in the resulting row.**
- An image captured on an iPhone arrives in storage resized (≤2000px on the
  longest axis), whatever format the phone offered.
- A user who is not signed in is sent to login and returned to `/capture`
  afterwards — including on first launch in standalone mode.
- Every existing route renders and behaves exactly as before the layout split.

## Risks

- **🔴 Session persistence in standalone mode is the main delivery risk.** An
  iOS home-screen web app has a storage container separate from Safari, so the
  user signs in again on first launch inside the installed app. How long that
  session then survives — across days of non-use, storage pressure, and Safari's
  storage policies — determines whether this design is pleasant or infuriating.
  **Spike this during P2, before building anything on top of it.** If sessions
  prove short-lived, the mitigation (biometric-gated re-auth, longer refresh
  tokens) is a design change, not a tweak.
- **🟠 No offline capture on iOS.** Safari does not support the Background Sync
  API. "Snap five receipts in a parking garage with no signal, pocket the phone,
  and have them upload later" **does not work on the web**, and no amount of
  service-worker effort makes it work. The best achievable is holding files in
  IndexedDB and retrying when the user next opens the app — which requires them
  to open it. **This is the single scenario that would justify revisiting D1.**
- **🟠 H3 gets a busier caller.** `/api/ocr/extract` is unauthenticated with no
  host allow-list on the caller-supplied `fileUrl`. This PRD does not create that
  hole, but a phone-friendly capture surface will drive materially more traffic
  through it. Fixing H3 is not a blocker for P1–P2 but should not lag far behind.
- **🟢 Layout split blast radius.** R2 touches the parent of every route. Low
  risk, but it is the change most likely to cause a broad regression, which is
  why it lands on its own (see Sequencing).

## Testing notes

Per project convention — unit tests own correctness, Playwright is seam-only:

# PRD — Mobile Capture (single-purpose receipt capture on a phone)

- **Status:** Draft
- **Created:** 2026-07-26
- **Surface:** a new chrome-free `/capture` route; a route-group split of
  `src/routes/+layout.svelte`; a web app manifest + icons in `static/`; a queued
  wrapper around the existing `ReceiptService.uploadAndCreate()`.
- **Related:**
  - Backlog **"iPhone camera"** feature — this PRD is its concrete design, and
    deliberately answers it with a web app rather than a native iOS app.
  - [Refactoring backlog](refactoring-backlog.md) — the layout split (D2) is a
    prerequisite, not a nice-to-have.
  - Security **H3** (`/api/ocr/extract` unauthenticated + SSRF) — not caused by
    this work, but this feature adds a second high-traffic consumer of that
    endpoint. See [Security Remediation PRD](prd-done/prd-security-remediation.md).
  - [domain-model.md](domain-model.md) — Receipt, Expense terminology.

## Terminology

See [domain-model.md](domain-model.md). A **Receipt** is a row in `receipts` plus
its stored image; an **Expense** is the computed join of a receipt with its
category. This PRD introduces no new domain concepts — only a second **client
surface** onto the existing receipt-creation pipeline.

Two new UI terms, both presentational:

- **Capture screen** — the `/capture` route: one job, no navigation.
- **Upload queue** — the client-side, in-memory (later persisted) list of files
  in flight, each with its own state. Not a database concept; nothing is queued
  server-side.

## Problem

The app is usable on a phone but was not designed for one. Every route inherits
the full navigation chrome, date filters, and desktop-density tables from
`src/routes/+layout.svelte` (143 lines). The receipts page is a management
console — list, sort, edit, split, reconcile — with upload as one control among
many.

That mismatch matters because the phone use case is not "manage receipts." It is
a single five-second task, performed standing up, one-handed, often on cellular,
immediately after a purchase: **photograph this receipt and make it go away.**
Anything that asks the user to navigate, scroll past a table, or wait for an
upload before taking the next shot is friction at exactly the wrong moment — and
the observable consequence is receipts that never get captured at all.

The naive fix is "make the app responsive." That is a large job and it does not
solve this problem: a responsive `/expenses` table is still a dense multi-column
grid, and the user standing at a till does not want it at any width.

The second naive fix is a native iOS app. Assessed and rejected for v1 — see
**D1**.

## Goals

- Capturing a receipt on a phone is: open icon → tap shutter → done. Five
  seconds, one hand, no navigation.
- Capturing **n** receipts in a row is **n** taps, not **n** upload-wait cycles.
- The capture surface shares one codebase, one deployment, one auth session, and
  one ingestion pipeline with the desktop app.
- The image that reaches storage is resized, regardless of what format the phone
  hands us.
- A failed upload is visible and retryable, never silent.

## Non-goals

- **A native iOS app.** Rejected for v1 (**D1**), with the one scenario that
  would justify it named explicitly under **Risks**.
- **Making the rest of the app responsive.** `/expenses`, `/spending`,
  `/transactions`, `/reconciliation` are unchanged and remain desktop surfaces.
  This PRD adds a route; it does not restyle existing ones.
- **Editing receipts on the phone.** No category assignment, no split, no
  reconciliation, no merchant correction beyond what **R6** decides. Review
  happens on the desktop app.
- **Offline capture.** Explicitly deferred to a later phase and constrained by a
  platform limit (**Risks**). v1 requires a live connection.
- **Changing the ingestion pipeline.** `uploadAndCreate()` keeps its current
  semantics — OCR fail-soft, orphan-blob cleanup, `withRetry`. This PRD wraps it,
  it does not rewrite it. (Moving the pipeline server-side into an Edge Function
  remains a good idea and a separate decision; it is **not** a prerequisite.)
- **Android.** The design is standards-based and should work, but iOS Safari is
  the only target verified.

## Design

### D1 — A PWA route, not a native app (the platform decision)

The existing receipts input (`src/routes/receipts/+page.svelte:489`) is already a
`<input type="file" accept="image/jpeg,image/png,image/heic,application/pdf"
multiple>`. On iOS Safari that already offers **Take Photo**, **Photo Library**,
and **Choose File**. The camera is not the missing capability — the
single-purpose surface is.

A web app manifest lets one codebase ship two products. With `start_url:
/capture` and `display: standalone`, the home-screen icon opens chrome-free,
directly on the capture screen, and never reveals the expenses table or the date
filters. The desktop app stays at the normal URL.

What a native app would add, and why each is insufficient here:

| Capability                          | Web        | Native | Verdict for v1 |
| ----------------------------------- | ---------- | ------ | -------------- |
| Camera capture / photo library      | ✅         | ✅     | No gain        |
| Home-screen icon, standalone chrome | ✅         | ✅     | No gain        |
| HEIC handling                       | ✅ (**D5**) | ✅     | No gain        |
| Share Extension (Photos → app)      | ❌         | ✅     | Real, deferred |
| Background upload                   | ❌         | ✅     | Real, deferred |
| Offline queue                       | ❌ (**Risks**) | ✅ | Real, deferred |
| Document scanner (auto-crop/deskew) | ❌         | ✅     | Real, deferred |

Against that: a native app costs an Apple Developer Program membership
($99/yr), a second toolchain, a second copy of the upload pipeline in Swift — a
third copy of logic that must stay in lock-step, which is the failure mode
`CLAUDE.md` already warns about for the Deno `supabase/functions/_shared/`
duplication — and TestFlight builds that expire every 90 days. The web route
costs one route and a manifest.

**Decision: build the web route.** Revisit natively only if the offline scenario
under **Risks** proves to be a real, recurring need.

### D2 — Route-group split so the capture screen has no chrome

`src/routes/+layout.svelte` currently owns three things at once: the auth gate
(`publicRoutes`, `authChecked`), the nav chrome, and `preserveFilters`. The
capture screen needs the first and none of the rest.

Two options:

- **(a) Route groups.** Move today's layout to `src/routes/(app)/+layout.svelte`
  and give the capture screen `src/routes/(capture)/+layout.svelte`. Auth
  handling is lifted into a shared root layout so it is not duplicated. Route
  groups do not affect URLs, so every existing path is unchanged.
- **(b) Conditional.** Keep one layout and hide the nav when the path starts with
  `/capture`.

**Recommend (a).** Option (b) is one line today and accretes a special case per
divergence — and this PRD is the first of what will be several: the capture
screen also wants a different viewport meta, different safe-area padding, and no
`preserveFilters` subscription. The auth-gate extraction is the only real work;
it is mechanical and independently testable.

### D3 — The screen: one shutter, immediate re-arm

The layout is deliberately impoverished:

- **A single large shutter control**, thumb-reachable in the lower third, using
  `capture="environment"` so it opens the camera **directly** — no intermediate
  sheet.
- **A smaller secondary control** for the photo library — the same input without
  the `capture` attribute, so iOS offers the picker.
- **Immediate re-arm.** Upload starts in the background and the shutter is ready
  again at once. This is the core interaction: capturing five receipts is five
  taps.
- **An upload-queue strip** below the shutter: a local thumbnail per item (from
  `URL.createObjectURL` — no signed-URL round trip), a state label, and
  tap-to-retry on failure.
- **Nothing else.** No nav, no filters, no table, no totals.

### D4 — The upload queue

`uploadAndCreate()` today is awaited per file, serially, with the page's
`uploading` boolean as the only feedback. The capture screen needs per-item state
and concurrency.

Each queue item carries: a client-generated id, the local object URL, and one of
`queued → uploading → extracting → done | failed` (plus the error message for
`failed`). The mapping onto the existing pipeline is direct — `uploading` covers
`prepareFileForUpload` + `uploadToStorage`, `extracting` covers
`extractReceiptDataFailSoft`, `done` is set after
`insertReceiptOrCleanupUpload` returns.

Two properties the existing pipeline already gives us and the queue must not
break: OCR failure still produces a receipt (fail-soft), and a failed insert
removes the uploaded blob (no orphans). A queue item that reaches `failed`
therefore has left nothing behind, and retry is safe.

Concurrency is capped (start at 2) so a burst of captures on cellular does not
saturate the connection and starve the shot in progress.

**The queue is presentation state, not business logic.** The state machine and
the concurrency policy are pure and unit-testable; the Svelte component renders
them. Do not put upload orchestration inside the component.

### D5 — HEIC must not bypass the resizer

`resizeImage()` returns the file untouched for anything that is not JPEG or PNG
(`src/lib/utils/imageResize.ts:71`), and `prepareFileForUpload()` skips the
resize call for the same set (`ReceiptService.ts:203`). Meanwhile the receipts
input opts **into** HEIC via its `accept` list.

The suspected consequence: iOS Safari transcodes a picked photo to JPEG when the
`accept` list excludes HEIC, and hands over the original HEIC when it is
included. If so, today's configuration selects the one path where a full-size
iPhone photo goes to storage and to Mistral **unresized** — roughly a 3MB upload
where a 400KB one would do, on the connection least able to afford it. It also
sits near the 5MB image ceiling in `validateFile()`
(`ReceiptService.ts:170`), so a large capture can be rejected outright.

**This is a hypothesis and must be verified on a real device before it is acted
on** (see **R1**). If confirmed, the capture screen omits `image/heic` from its
`accept` list so iOS converts to JPEG and the file flows through the existing
resizer. The desktop receipts page keeps HEIC in its list — a Mac user may
legitimately upload a `.heic` file, and there the size and bandwidth cost is not
a concern.

Note the asymmetry this creates: two `accept` lists for two surfaces, for a
stated reason. Comment it at both sites.

### D6 — Installability

A manifest (`static/manifest.webmanifest`) with `name`, `short_name`,
`start_url: /capture`, `display: standalone`, theme/background colours, and the
icon set; plus `apple-touch-icon` and viewport/safe-area meta in `app.html`.

**No service worker is required for v1.** iOS supports Add to Home Screen and
honours `display: standalone` from the manifest without one. A service worker is
introduced only if and when offline persistence (P4) is built — adding one
earlier buys nothing and brings a cache-invalidation problem the app does not
currently have.

## Requirements

### R1 — Verify the HEIC hypothesis (do this first)

On a real iPhone, capture through the current receipts input and record: the
`File.type` and `File.size` the browser hands over, whether `prepareFileForUpload`
resizes, and the bytes that land in storage. Repeat with `image/heic` removed
from `accept`. **D5** is contingent on this result; if the behaviour differs from
the hypothesis, revise D5 rather than implementing it as written.

### R2 — Layout split

Per **D2(a)**. Auth gate extracted to a shared root layout; existing nav chrome
and `preserveFilters` move to `(app)`; a minimal `(capture)` layout. No URL
changes, no behaviour change to any existing route.

### R3 — `/capture` route

Per **D3**. Shutter (`capture="environment"`), library control, queue strip,
no chrome. Must render correctly with the on-screen keyboard absent and respect
iOS safe-area insets.

### R4 — Upload queue

Per **D4**. Pure state machine + concurrency policy; component renders it.
Reuses `ReceiptService.uploadAndCreate()` unchanged.

### R5 — Manifest and icons

Per **D6**. Installs to the home screen, opens standalone on `/capture`.

### R6 — Post-capture feedback

**Open — see Open Questions 1.** The default assumed by this PRD is
fire-and-forget: the queue strip is the only feedback, plus a passive count of
receipts awaiting review that deep-links into the desktop app. If inline OCR
confirmation is chosen instead, R6 grows substantially and P3 should be
re-estimated.

## Acceptance criteria

  browser or app navigation chrome visible.
- Tapping the shutter opens the camera directly — no intermediate action sheet.
- After taking a photo, the shutter is usable again before the upload completes.
  Five receipts can be captured in five taps without waiting.
- Each queued item shows a thumbnail and its current state; a failed item shows
  an error and can be retried, and retrying succeeds once connectivity returns.
- A receipt captured on the phone appears in the desktop `/expenses` list with
  the same family scoping, auto-categorisation, and `suspicious_date` behaviour
  as one uploaded from the desktop. **No divergence in the resulting row.**
- An image captured on an iPhone arrives in storage resized (≤2000px on the
  longest axis), whatever format the phone offered.
- A user who is not signed in is sent to login and returned to `/capture`
  afterwards — including on first launch in standalone mode.
- Every existing route renders and behaves exactly as before the layout split.

## Risks

- **🔴 Session persistence in standalone mode is the main delivery risk.** An
  iOS home-screen web app has a storage container separate from Safari, so the
  user signs in again on first launch inside the installed app. How long that
  session then survives — across days of non-use, storage pressure, and Safari's
  storage policies — determines whether this design is pleasant or infuriating.
  **Spike this during P2, before building anything on top of it.** If sessions
  prove short-lived, the mitigation (biometric-gated re-auth, longer refresh
  tokens) is a design change, not a tweak.
- **🟠 No offline capture on iOS.** Safari does not support the Background Sync
  API. "Snap five receipts in a parking garage with no signal, pocket the phone,
  and have them upload later" **does not work on the web**, and no amount of
  service-worker effort makes it work. The best achievable is holding files in
  IndexedDB and retrying when the user next opens the app — which requires them
  to open it. **This is the single scenario that would justify revisiting D1.**
- **🟠 H3 gets a busier caller.** `/api/ocr/extract` is unauthenticated with no
  host allow-list on the caller-supplied `fileUrl`. This PRD does not create that
  hole, but a phone-friendly capture surface will drive materially more traffic
  through it. Fixing H3 is not a blocker for P1–P2 but should not lag far behind.
- **🟢 Layout split blast radius.** R2 touches the parent of every route. Low
  risk, but it is the change most likely to cause a broad regression, which is
  why it lands on its own (see Sequencing).

## Testing notes

Per project convention — unit tests own correctness, Playwright is seam-only:

- **Unit:** the queue state machine (transitions, retry-after-failure,
  concurrency cap, ordering) as pure logic with the Supabase client mocked at the
  boundary. Any `accept`-list or format-selection helper introduced by D5.
- **Render:** the capture component against a stubbed queue — shutter present and
  re-armed, per-item states, retry affordance.
- **Playwright seam:** one thin flow proving the route is wired (file input →
  `uploadAndCreate` → receipt row), plus a regression pass that existing routes
  still render after the layout split. Not a device matrix.
- **Manual, on a real iPhone — unavoidable and not optional.** R1's format
  investigation, standalone-mode install and session survival, safe-area layout,
  and the camera-opens-directly behaviour cannot be verified in CI or a
  simulator. Record the results in this PRD as they are established.

## Open questions

1. **Does the capture screen show OCR results, or is it fire-and-forget?** The
   biggest fork, and it gates R6. OCR takes several seconds via Mistral, so

   twenty-second one. Fire-and-forget is faster and much simpler, but pushes the
   `suspicious_date` flag and every OCR miss into a later session on another
   device — possibly never. **Recommend fire-and-forget for v1**, with a passive
   "n receipts need review" count. Reverse this if receipts routinely go
   unreviewed today.
2. **Route group or conditional nav?** **Recommend the route group (D2a).**
3. **Is the user willing to install to the home screen?** The design assumes yes.
   Opening `/capture` in a Safari tab still works but keeps browser chrome and
   loses the standalone feel — a materially worse product for the same build.
4. **Multi-shot batching.** Should the library control allow selecting many
   photos at once (the desktop input already sets `multiple`), or is
   one-at-a-time the right mobile default? Leaning `multiple` — it costs nothing
   and the queue already handles n items.
5. **PDF on mobile.** The desktop accepts PDFs up to 10MB. Does the capture
   screen offer them at all? Leaning no for v1 — "Choose File" clutters a screen
   whose entire premise is one tap.

## Sequencing

Each phase is independently shippable and leaves the app no worse.

1. **P1 — R1 (verify HEIC) and R2 (layout split).** Investigation plus the
   riskiest structural change, landed alone so a regression is unambiguous. No
   user-visible feature yet.
2. **P2 — R3 + R4 (the capture screen) and the standalone-session spike.** Usable
   end-to-end at `/capture` in a browser tab. **Run the session spike before
   building on top of it.**
3. **P3 — R5 (manifest, icons) and R6 (feedback, per OQ1).** The point at which
   it becomes a product rather than a route.
4. **P4 — queue durability.** IndexedDB persistence so a mid-upload app switch
   does not lose the shot, plus retry-on-reopen. This is the honest limit of the
   web platform on iOS; do not promise offline capture beyond it.

document scanner — all native-only, all revisited together if and only if the
offline scenario proves real.
